request: Design simple locking mechanism in the area of the hook to secure carried load.

parameters.mechanism_type: Normally closed, inward-opening, spring-return safety gate assembled to the existing hook end.
parameters.existing_model_modification: Add a transverse hinge bore through the narrow end of the tapered lever arm immediately adjacent to the hook throat. Preserve the hook seat and load-bearing heel.
parameters.gate_configuration: Use a forked gate with two external side cheeks straddling the existing part and a transverse bridge at the free end. The bridge closes the open hook throat and bears against the terminal nose in the closed position.
parameters.pivot_axis: Orient the gate pivot axis parallel to the existing clevis pivot-bore axis and normal to the longitudinal side faces, approximately along the global y direction.
parameters.preliminary_hinge_pin_diameter: 3 mm nominal; finalize from material strength, carried-load rating, fatigue requirement, and available edge ligament.
parameters.minimum_pivot_edge_ligament: At least 1.5 times the finalized hinge-pin diameter from the bore edge to the nearest free profile edge, subject to stress verification.
parameters.running_clearance: Provide approximately 0.10 to 0.20 mm diametral clearance between the gate hinge bore and pin for a free-running joint, adjusted for manufacturing process.
parameters.side_clearance: Provide approximately 0.20 to 0.30 mm clearance per side between the existing lever and the two gate cheeks.
parameters.closed_tip_clearance: Use a small non-jamming clearance, approximately 0.20 to 0.50 mm, between the gate stop profile and the terminal nose under nominal conditions.
parameters.opening_behavior: The gate must rotate inward toward the hook seat when a load is inserted and return automatically to the closed position after the load passes the throat.
parameters.closed_stop: Contour the free end of the gate to stop against the inner-facing region of the terminal nose cylinder rather than against the concave load seat.
parameters.preserved_geometry: Do not remove or reduce the radius-3 concave engagement seat or the radius-9 outer heel because these faces provide the principal load-bearing and load-transfer paths.
parameters.symmetry: Keep the gate and hinge centered about the model longitudinal mid-plane y=0 and maintain balanced loading on both sides of the hook.
parameters.finish: Round or chamfer exposed gate edges and fillet the gate-arm-to-hub transitions to remove insertion snags and reduce stress concentration.

actions.target: The area of the existing hook.
actions.relational_constraint: The locking mechanism must be located in the area of the hook.
actions.unresolved_reference: The hook is localized as SEC_03 at the positive-x end. The preferred hinge location is the adjacent narrow end of SEC_02. Final gate thickness, hinge diameter, spring torque, allowable opening angle, material, manufacturing clearances, load envelope, proof-load rating, and required safety factor remain unspecified and require engineering validation.
steps: Localize the locking region at SEC_03, the Hook catch end, at the narrow positive-x end shown on the right side of the front view. Treat the radius-3 concave engagement seat face 0011, Brep FACE 7, as protected load-bearing geometry and use it to define the retained-load envelope.

Identify the open throat between the upper throat transition face 0012, Brep FACE 8, and the upright terminal nose. Use the terminal nose cylinder face 0014, Brep FACE 13, as the closed-gate reaction and stop reference. Use terminal nose cap face 0013, Brep FACE 17, as a vertical-height reference, but avoid placing the primary stop directly on its exposed top surface.
Preserve the hook outer heel face 0015, Brep FACE 10. This radius-9 convex surface transfers engagement loads into SEC_02 and should not be drilled, pocketed, or reduced for the locking mechanism.

Create or activate the longitudinal symmetry datum plane y=0. Establish a transverse hinge axis parallel to the existing clevis bore axis and normal to negative-side arm face 0008, Brep FACE 9, and positive-side arm face 0010, Brep FACE 16.

Place the hinge axis in the narrow positive-x end of SEC_02 immediately behind the hook throat transition. Locate it below the upper sloped arm face 0007, Brep FACE 5, far enough from the upper and lower profile edges to maintain at least 1.5 pin diameters of edge ligament. Confirm that the bore does not intersect face 0011, face 0012, or face 0015.

On side face 0008 or on a parallel datum plane, sketch the hinge-bore circle concentric with the established axis. Apply a through-all symmetric cut across the full y width so that the bore exits side face 0010. Use a nominal 3 mm hinge diameter only as a preliminary value and resize it after load and bearing-stress calculations.

If required by the selected pin and spring arrangement, add shallow concentric spotfaces on faces 0008 and 0010. Keep the spotfaces minimal and symmetric, and do not create a recess that materially weakens the tapered arm-to-hook transition.

Create NEW_SEC_04 as a separate pivoting safety-gate component. On a plane parallel to face 0008, sketch one gate cheek with a circular pivot hub, a tapered arm following the external hook profile, and a rounded free end extending across the open throat toward face 0014.

Dimension the gate cheek so it remains outside the existing side face with approximately 0.20 to 0.30 mm running clearance. Maintain clearance from upper throat transition face 0012 throughout the opening motion and prevent the cheek from entering the radius-3 concave seat represented by face 0011.

Extrude the first gate cheek to the selected plate thickness. Mirror it about the y=0 symmetry plane to create the opposite cheek. Join the two cheeks at their free ends with a transverse bridge so that the resulting gate is forked around the existing hook body and closes the throat across the full part width.

Shape the free-end bridge with a rounded insertion surface and a complementary stop surface directed toward terminal nose cylinder face 0014. In the closed state, provide a small non-jamming clearance while ensuring that an outward-moving carried load contacts the gate before it can escape through the throat.

Add coaxial hinge bores through both gate hubs. Align these bores with the new transverse bore through SEC_02. Provide the specified running clearance between the gate and hinge pin, and provide axial side clearance so the gate rotates freely without rubbing faces 0008 or 0010.

Create NEW_SEC_05 as a transverse cylindrical hinge pin passing through the first gate cheek, the modified SEC_02 hinge bore, and the opposite gate cheek. Retain the pin with suitable end heads, staking, circlips, or another process-compatible retention feature while keeping the assembly substantially symmetric about y=0.

Create NEW_SEC_06 as a torsion return spring around the hinge pin. Seat one spring leg against the gate and the other against a non-critical region near upper arm face 0007. Set the spring preload so the gate is normally closed against its nose-side stop but can be pushed inward manually or by the entering load.

Add a rotational limit or gate-hub stop that prevents the gate from rotating outward beyond the closed position. Permit sufficient inward rotation for the intended mating pin, edge, cable, or catch element to pass through the throat without colliding with face 0011.

Apply fillets at the gate hub-to-arm transitions and round the bridge edges exposed to insertion. Add small manufacturing chamfers to the hinge bores and pin ends. Avoid sharp edges adjacent to the carried load or spring.

Assemble the gate, pin, and spring with concentric constraints at the hinge axis. Center the forked gate about y=0, apply a rotational degree of freedom, and define closed and fully open angular limits.

Perform swept-volume and interference checks through the complete gate rotation. Verify clearance to faces 0011, 0012, 0013, 0014, 0015, 0007, 0008, and 0010, including worst-case manufacturing tolerance and spring deflection.

Validate the closed configuration from the front, back, top, bottom, right, and isometric views. Confirm that the gate visibly bridges the throat, cannot be forced outward by the carried load, and does not obstruct seating against face 0011.

Complete bearing, shear, bending, fatigue, and contact checks for the hinge bore, pin, gate cheeks, terminal-nose stop, and SEC_02-to-SEC_03 transition. Increase pin diameter, gate thickness, local hub radius, or edge ligament as required without modifying the concave seat or outer heel load paths.
